ai.description: *Minervarya marathi* is a small frog (22–26 mm) with a brown dorsum and dark lateral markings. It is distinguished by a prominent, white, longitudinal mid-dorsal stripe and smooth ventral skin.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Minervarya marathi* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous, and prominent glandular fold (dorsolateral ridge) that extends from the eye to the groin.
ai.habitat: *Minervarya marathi* inhabits the northern Western Ghats, typically found in open grasslands, agricultural fields, and near temporary monsoon pools at low to mid-altitudes.
ai.behavior: *Minervarya marathi* is primarily nocturnal, emerging during the monsoon season to forage for small insects and invertebrates in damp, grassy habitats.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Minervarya marathi* is an oviparous frog that breeds during the monsoon season (June–August), laying clutches of approximately 200–300 eggs in shallow water bodies.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Minervarya marathi* is endemic to the northern Western Ghats in the Indian state of Maharashtra, typically found at elevations between 500 and 1,200 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Minervarya marathi* consists of a series of rapid, high-pitched, metallic "tink" notes, typically emitted from shallow, rain-filled roadside ditches.
